B.bigcommerce:
Good tracking shows which ads produce sales, so you can put more money behind what works. When sales are missing or miscounted, you make those calls on bad numbers, and Google Ads learns from them too. This setup gives GA4 and Google Ads a cleaner record of what people view, add to cart and buy.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.universal:
If you run ads, you need to know how many real leads they produce. Counting button clicks can include people who never finished the form, so your numbers can look better than they are. This setup counts confirmed form submissions, and one script covers nine form tools, so you don't need a different setup for each site.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.gravityforms:
If your site uses Gravity Forms, this helps you trust your lead numbers. It counts a lead once the form confirms it, not when someone clicks a button. It also gives Google Ads better contact details to match leads to your ads, which gives its bidding better information to learn from.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.wpforms:
If your site uses WPForms, this helps you trust your lead numbers. It counts a lead once the form confirms it, not when someone clicks a button. Because it finds each field by its label, the lead's contact details reach Google Ads correctly on any form.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.jotform:
If your Jotform sends people to a thank-you page, a common setup counts every reload of that page as a new lead. That makes your ads look better than they are. This setup counts the submission without counting those reloads, so your lead numbers are closer to what your sales team actually gets.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.squarespace:
If your site is on Squarespace, you need to know which ads bring in enquiries. This setup counts a lead once Squarespace confirms it received the form, and passes the name, email and phone to Google Ads so it can match leads to your ads. That gives you lead numbers you can trust more.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.swipepages:
If you send ad traffic to a SwipePages landing page, you need to know how many leads that page produces. This setup counts leads once SwipePages confirms them, and can keep them separate from your main website. Then you can see which one is earning your ad spend.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
B.gohighlevel:
If your GoHighLevel page has a form and a calendar, you want to know which is which. This setup counts form leads and leaves out bookings, so your form numbers aren't inflated by them. It also passes contact details to Google Ads so it can match leads to your ads.

The steps below are for whoever installs it, so you can hand this page to your developer or marketer.
